get.description: Durable, ordered feed of permit.created (first seen by our crawler) and permit.changed (one published field changed on a re-pull) events since 2026-10-12; there is no older change history. Backfill created events (older records loaded with a newly connected source) are left out unless include_backfill=true. Events come in seq order, which is time order; pass next_cursor back as since to resume without missing or repeating an event, and keep paging while has_more is true (a page scans at most 100,000 events, so a narrow filter can return a short or empty page). Metered: one record per event. An organization with an area feed reads only that feed: the rows are free and an organization with no feed area gets 403 feature_requires_area_feed.

get.description: The bulk export releases, newest first: base snapshots (every table) and incrementals (since the previous release: full rows of new or changed permits with their permit_versions hashes, last_seen of permits re-pulled unchanged, permit deletes, the tag rows of changed permits and the change-feed events), each with its manifest (schema, row counts, sha256 per file, data release, seq window). Every file carries a signed `url` valid for the calling key only, until expires_at. Free: listing charges no records; a download charges the rows in the file. An enforced organization needs an area feed (403 feature_requires_area_feed without one, matching features.bulk_exports in GET /v1/entitlements) and its downloads are free. The country feed sees every file; a state, metro or county feed sees only the partitions its feed touches, with `scope` on each release, and files filtered to its feed agencies (or counties) are marked `scoped` with `rows` null until downloaded.

get.description: Search permits. Every /v0/permits filter with the same meaning plus geo_id, address and property IDs, ZIP, tags (with -tag exclusion), contractor license, has_contractor and has_value, the event date window date_from/date_to (date_issued, else date_applied, else record_date; the default way to search a date window), finaled and Shovels-style permit date windows, minimum approval and construction days, and include_count. By default the search returns every permit class except the non-construction ones (admin, business_license, code_enforcement, engineering_row, environmental_health, other, planning); pass category=all for every class. All filters are ANDed. Items are v1 permit objects: id first, the issuer's fields with source_url and provenance, then approval_days, construction_days and total_days, contractor_link, and description_derived with description_derived_sources (null unless the permit's own description is missing, a code or shorthand and a model wrote one; the issuer's description is never replaced). Keyset paginated with next_cursor. The permit object ends with agency_name: the place the agency key serves, '<jurisdiction name>, <state>' from the agency's jurisdiction (for example bridgeport_tx -> 'Bridgeport, CT'); null when the agency has no jurisdiction. excluded_classes lists the classes the default scope left out (empty unless no category was given). Metered: one record per item. within=entitled narrows the search to the organization's area feed. An organization's feed rows are free and need no Developer records; rows outside it are charged to the Developer meter, and a response that cannot pay for them answers 402 with areas_needed (the areas that would cover them), coverage_building (the api_only areas those rows sit in, where no feed is sold yet) and upgrade_url. X-BA-Scope on the response says feed, metered or mixed.

post.description: Subscribe an https URL to the change feed (GET /v1/changes) with a filter: geo_id, tags, types, fields, include_backfill, backfill. As in GET /v1/changes, backfill created events are left out unless the filter sets include_backfill: true. The response carries the signing secret once; every delivery is a POST of up to 100 events in seq order with X-PermitIntel-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>." + body)>. Private, loopback and link-local targets are refused. The subscription belongs to the calling key; a key may have at most 5 active webhooks (plans config), and one more answers 403 forbidden. Not metered; each delivered event counts as one record for the key, once, and plan fair-use caps pause deliveries (GET /v1/usage shows it). An organization whose plan is enforced may subscribe when it holds an area feed, even though its Developer plan's webhooks flag is false: the feed grants them and the worker delivers only events inside the feed. Without a feed area it answers 403 feature_requires_area_feed.
